newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices extend gains with heat.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices extend gains with heat.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices gained more ground Tuesday as temperatures near 100 degrees F blanketed many parts of the U.S., sources said.
On the Louisiana Gulf Coast, prices were quoted about three cents higher at $2.20-2.22 per mmBtu at the Henry Hub.
Similarly in south Texas prices gained four cents to about $2.15.
However, forecasts calling for cooler weather later this week will likely put a lid on the price rally, traders said.
In the Permian Basin market, prices climbed to $2.11-2.14, up another four cents from Monday.
Southern California border prices were about two cents firmer in the mid-$2.20s, but the restart of the 1,070 megawatt (MW) San Onofre 2 nuclear unit tempered a significant rally.
The adjacent unit 3, rated at 1,080 MW, was expected to resume power output Thursday, according to the Nuclear Regulatory Commission.
San Juan prices were quoted at $2.06-2.11, while Waha values edged to about $2.15.
The 750 MW unit 5 at the Four Corners coal plant in New Mexico was still off line for nearly three weeks of repairs.
In the Midwest, swing prices gained four cents to about $2.09-2.10. Chicago city-gate prices were quoted equally firmer in the high-$2.20s to low-$2.30s.
In the East, swing prices at the New York city-gate also rose several cents to the low-to-mid $2.50s.
